title: Abdominal Pain

rationale.CBC / BMP: Hemoconcentration if dehydrated. AKI from volume loss.
rationale.Oral rehydration / IV fluids: Mainstay. ORS preferred if able to tolerate PO.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with acute onset nausea, vomiting, diffuse abdominal cramping, watery diarrhea, and low-grade fever. History reveals recent consumption of undercooked food or potential contaminated source. Most common causes: S. aureus (preformed toxin, 1-6h onset), B. cereus, C. perfringens, Salmonella, Campylobacter, Shigella, E. coli. Most cases are self-limited (viral or toxin-mediated). Key: assess hydration status. Stool culture if: bloody diarrhea, severe illness, immunocompromised, >3 days, recent antibiotics or hospitalization. Treatment: supportive — oral rehydration (or IV fluids if severe). Antiemetics (ondansetron), loperamide if non-bloody diarrhea and no fever (avoid in dysentery — can prolong illness). Empiric antibiotics only for severe cases, bloody diarrhea, immunocompromised (fluoroquinolone or azithromycin).
